Status update — initial findings (14:22 PDT):

Summary: We see a combination of KV cache churn and a change in sequence-length distribution from OrbitRx's recent client push; that increased overall token processing per-request and evicted hot cache entries. As a result, tail latency climbed and we started hitting gateway timeouts while backend workers backed up. No evidence of a new deploy in our infra in the past 6 hours.

Evidence:
- Sample logs (attached in diagnostic_dump_1014.tar.gz) show repeated cache misses for model: rdx-3b-quant at 13:51:02
- Kernel logs indicate increased average sequence length from ~128 to ~640 for a subset of requests
- Per-host CPU/GPU utilization increased ~15% on the dedicated pool serving OrbitRx traffic

Immediate mitigation options:
A) Enable a short-lived prefix/KV sticky cache for OrbitRx (requires runtime toggle; ~4–6m to apply and verify)
B) Route high-cost requests to a cheaper-but-compatible model variant (rdx-3b-fast) to keep latency under SLO — potential quality regression (we can A/B some traffic)
C) Temporarily raise autoscale burst cap for OrbitRx dedicated pool (costly) — quick but expensive

I recommend we do A + B in parallel: enable sticky cache and route >512-token requests to rdx-3b-fast with a 10% sample fallback to rdx-3b-quant to monitor regression. I can kick off toggles now if we get approvals.

Attachments: diagnostic_dump_1014.tar.gz (logs), slo-mitigation-playbook.pdf (ops steps).

-Neha
